tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a scheduled task. At each occurrence of rrule, prompt is delivered to the target session as a scheduled message from the user. The result includes the task id and the next occurrence as scheduledAt in UTC and scheduledAtLocal in the zone of rrule. After downtime, only the latest missed occurrence is delivered. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

title.description: Task name of at most 120 characters in the user's language: action plus object. Omit timing, status, ids, and bracketed suffixes.

rrule.description: Supported RFC 5545 subset: one DTSTART line, a newline, and one RRULE line. DTSTART ends in Z for UTC or carries TZID with an IANA time zone; a fixed offset such as UTC+5 is Etc/GMT-5, with the sign reversed. DTSTART must name an existing local time. A TZID rule keeps local clock time across daylight-saving changes; generated nonexistent local times are skipped, and repeated ones occur once, at the earlier instant. DTSTART may be in the past; delivery starts with the first occurrence after creation. A one-time delivery is RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1. No SECONDLY; BYSECOND takes one value. COUNT is at most 1000; use UNTIL for longer rules. MINUTELY and HOURLY accept no BY parts, so select clock times with DAILY or WEEKLY plus BYHOUR and BYMINUTE. BYMONTHDAY and ordinal BYDAY require MONTHLY or YEARLY; BYYEARDAY and BYWEEKNO require YEARLY. Ordinal BYDAY cannot combine with BYWEEKNO. Each FREQ period allows at most 10080 candidates before BYSETPOS, which accepts at most 31 values. UNTIL is a UTC instant ending in Z. Example: "DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Singapore:20260901T080000\nRRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1"

target.description: this_session delivers to this session; new_once delivers to the same new session every time, opened at the first delivery; new opens a different new session for every delivery. New sessions use this session's working directory and preset. With this_session or new_once, a delivery waits until the previous one finishes, and only the latest occurrence that passed meanwhile is delivered. Use this_session for reminders and for follow-ups to this conversation; use new_once or new for independent work, such as a recurring report, and whenever the user asks for a new conversation.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

Good — model DDL matches migration names and index definitions. Column key for metadata is "metadata" (because name given? Interesting — Print shows `metadata -> metadata`, so key == name; the mapped attribute is metadata_, but the table column key is the DB name). So the GIN index resolves correctly.

Wait — this is important for the model: attribute `metadata_` maps to column with key "metadata". Does ORM querying/`session.get` work? Test `test_metadata_attribute_roundtrips_jsonb` passes per report. Fine.

Also note chunk id column type prints CHAR(32) for generic dialect display but with postgres dialect compile it's UUID (sa.Uuid compiles as UUID). The schema test asserts udt_name uuid; report says passed. Let me quickly verify with postgres dialect compile of CreateTable for both to confirm `UUID` and timestamptz, server defaults. Let me do that as part of the same focused check for model↔migration agreement. Actually, the model Uuid compiles to UUID in postgres. Fine, and tests introspect real DB.

One thing to verify: does the model's `mapped_column(Vector(_EMBEDDING_DIM))` render `vector(1536)`? Output shows VECTOR(1536) ✅.

Now let me compare model DDL with migration DDL more carefully for column-level differences that tests wouldn't catch? Tests introspect live DB built by create_all; migration separately verified by report's schema diff. I can compile the model's CreateTable and compare to migration's op.create_table — I can eyeball:

Model:
- id: uuid PK default client-side uuid4 (migration sa.Uuid() nullable=False) ✅
- owner_user_id FK cascade ✅
- title String(200) not null ✅

- chunk_count Integer ✅

- created_at/updated_at timestamptz not null now() ✅

Migration same. Good.

Chunks:
- id ✅
- document_id uuid not null FK cascade ✅
- chunk_index int not null ✅
- content text not null ✅
- embedding vector(dim) not null ✅
- token_count int not null default 0 ✅
- metadata jsonb ✅
- created_at timestamptz not null now() ✅
- no updated_at ✅
- unique constraint ✅, HNSW ✅, GIN ✅

Now: are there differences in index *order* or DDL that matter? No.

One notable difference: `ix_knowledge_documents_owner` in model: `Index(..., "owner_user_id", text("updated_at DESC"))` compiles to `(owner_user_id, updated_at DESC)` ✅ matches migration.

Now consider the global constraint "迁移必须在开头 CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector" ✅ line 53 of diff.

"downgrade() 不得回退扩展" ✅.

Conftest env vars: 4 present ✅. `_TABLES` updated ✅. No Task 8 fixtures ✅ (diff shows none added; fixture list unchanged).

Now remaining review concerns to raise:

### A. `os.environ.setdefault` vs "强制" (force)
Conftest uses setdefault, meaning a developer with `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai` or `STORAGE_BACKEND=s3` exported in their shell would leak real backend into tests → zero-network/zero-external-storage guarantee breaks. However, existing conftest pattern is setdefault throughout (including LLM_PROVIDER=fake), and .env is overridden because env vars take precedence over .env in pydantic-settings. The global constraint wording says "conftest 强制". Is setdefault acceptable? The brief's §1.4 in report claims setdefault 会压过 .env — true. But shell env would not be overridden. For a test suite requirement "零网络、零外部存储", if someone has STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 in shell env, tests hit S3. Hmm. But LLM_PROVIDER=fake is also setdefault in existing code, so this is the established convention and the "force" in the constraint probably refers to "conftest sets these defaults". I'd call this Minor (defense-in-depth: use direct assignment for these 4, as they're test-only safety rails). Actually wait — does TEST_DATABASE_URL need to be respected? They set DATABASE_URL via setdefault from TEST_DATABASE_URL, so assignment directly would be wrong there. For ENGINE, direct assignment `os.environ["STORAGE_BACKEND"]="local"=...` is safe since tests must never use real storage. Minor.

But let me check whether `STORAGE_BACKEND`/`EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`/`KNOWLEDGE_DIR` settings even exist in config (Task 1/2 may have added them; this is Task 4, with tasks 1-3 presumably done). If `STORAGE_BACKEND` isn't a Settings field, pydantic might ignore (extra="ignore") and setting env is harmless/noise. But spec says Task 4 requires them. Quick grep config for these fields to note whether the env names are correct spellings (e.g., `STORAGE_BACKEND` vs `STORAGE_BACKEND`? and `KNOWLEDGE_DIR`). This is a concrete risk: wrong env var names make the conftest change a no-op. Let me grep.

### B. `.env` EMBEDDING_DIM not forced
Report notes conftest doesn't force `EMBEDDING_DIM`. If .env changes dim while the test DB has an existing table with old dim, `create_all` won't alter → all 13 model tests would fail with vector dim mismatch (or test_embedding_dimension_follows_settings fails). Actually more subtly, tests assert against `get_settings().embedding_dim` so most tests self-consistent; `test_embedding_dimension_follows_settings` would fail if DB table was created with a different dim. Since conftest doesn't force EMBEDDING_DIM, a dev's .env with EMBEDDING_DIM=1024 after the table was created at 1536 → failure. Not forcing it is per brief (only 4 vars), so this is a reporting note, not a defect. But is it a genuine risk to mention as Minor? The task brief explicitly limits to 4 env vars; R4 says only env vars listed... The brief lists 4. So not forcing EMBEDDING_DIM is compliant. I'll mention as ⚠️/Minor observation maybe.

Hmm wait, actually there could be a more concrete problem: the fake embedding provider — if Task 2's fake provider generates vectors based on `embedding_dim`, fine. Not this task's concern.

### C. Tests use `_chunk_count` global 0 assertions
Fragile if a previous test leaks (e.g. `test_metadata...` commits, but teardown truncates). Actually teardown truncates after each test, so within the suite it's fine. But note that if an individual test fails before teardown? Teardown still runs (yield fixture). If test raises, teardown still executes. So OK. 1. **[tests/conftest.py:34-37](tests/conftest.py#L34-L37) 用的是 `setdefault`，不是硬性覆盖，与「强制」措辞有落差。**
   问题：`.env` 已被环境变量优先级压过（正常情况有效），但若开发者 shell 里 `export EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai` / `STORAGE_BACKEND=s3` / `EMBEDDING_API_KEY=...`，`setdefault` 不会覆盖，测试会真的走外部存储/网络，直接破坏「测试零网络、零外部存储」这条硬约束。
   修复：这 4 个变量都是测试专用安全闸，建议直接赋值（`os.environ["STORAGE_BACKEND"] = "local"` 等）；`DATABASE_URL` 保持 `setdefault` 以尊重 `TEST_DATABASE_URL`。若团队坚持与既有 `LLM_PROVIDER` 风格统一，至少在注释中说明该残留风险。

2. **[tests/integration/test_knowledge_models.py:138-148](tests/integration/test_knowledge_models.py#L138-L148) 的维度测试在当前环境下几乎是自证。**
   问题：断言 `format_type == f"vector({get_settings().embedding_dim})"`，而模型列也由同一个 `get_settings()` 得出；conftest 未覆盖 `EMBEDDING_DIM`，默认 1536，此时若代码写死 1536 该测试**照样通过**，与报告「证明确实读配置而非写死 1536」的表述不符。
   修复：用非默认维度运行（如子进程设 `EMBEDDING_DIM=1024` 后 `create_all` 到临时 schema，断言 `vector(1024)`），或断言一个与默认值不同的常量。

   修复：修正报告措辞即可；若想真正验证 relationship 级联，可在测试内断言删除时 ORM 发出了子行 DELETE（或在 FK 暂时不可用/禁用的场景下验证）。
